gen.title: How a field pH meter produces a reading

steps.label: Place sample in collection cup
steps.quote: To use the pH meter in the photograph below, the water sample is placed in the cup

steps.label: Lower glass probe into water
steps.quote: the glass probe at the end of the retractable arm is placed in the water

steps.label: Electrodes detect voltage in bulb
steps.quote: Inside the thin glass bulb at the end of the probe there are two electrodes that measure voltage

steps.label: Reference electrode keeps fixed acidity
steps.quote: One electrode is contained in a liquid that has a fixed acidity, or pH

steps.label: Sample electrode senses water acidity
steps.quote: The other electrode responds to the acidity of the water sample

steps.label: Voltmeter measures voltage difference
steps.quote: A voltmeter in the probe measures the difference between the voltages of the two electrodes

steps.label: Meter converts voltage to display
steps.quote: The meter then translates the voltage difference into pH and displays it on the little screen on the main box
